newsitem.title: USA: U.S. heartened by moves to end Ecuador crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. heartened by moves to end Ecuador crisis.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it was "heartened" by the willingness of Ecuador's political leaders to resolve the country's crisis peacefully and praised the military's role as honourable.
Referring to a military-backed deal to resolve the crisis, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the adminstration would withhold final judgment until the agreement was concluded.
But "we are heartened by the willingness of these major political figures to seek a solution to this crisis in Ecuador," he said.

"We were heartened by the fact that the military and the national police had essentially allowed the politicians to work out what appears to be a political compromise...an agreement in principle that would retain politcal stability," he said.
As for the military, he said: "We think the military has acted honourably, at least so far."
Ecuador faced new political uncertainty on Monday because interim President Rosalia Arteaga raised doubts about the deal under which she would hand over power to the head of Congress.

Arteaga was appointed head of a caretaker government on Sunday as part of an agreement between lawmakers and the armed forces to end the crisis that erupted on Thursday when flamboyant populist President Abdala Bucaram was ousted by a divided Congress on grounds of "mental incompetence."
Burns acknowledged that Congress needed to sort through "ambiguities" and that "some remaining aspects (of the deal) need to be put into place."
